lines.text: Own a stock that goes bankrupt? Shareholders get paid dead last.

lines.text: S&P Global counted 785 large US corporate bankruptcies in 2025, the most since 2010.
lines.say: S and P Global counted seven hundred eighty-five large US corporate bankruptcies in twenty twenty-five, the most since twenty ten.

lines.text: The SEC's payout line: secured creditors, then unsecured creditors like bondholders, then stockholders last.
lines.say: The S E C's payout line: secured creditors, then unsecured creditors like bondholders, then stockholders last.

lines.text: In Chapter 11, the plan often cancels old shares and hands new stock to creditors.
lines.say: In Chapter eleven, the plan often cancels old shares and hands new stock to creditors.

lines.text: Our math: 100 shares at $20 is $2,000. If they're cancelled, that's $0.
lines.say: Our math: one hundred shares at twenty dollars is two thousand dollars. If they're cancelled, that's zero.

lines.text: Lehman filed in 2008; its shares were cancelled in 2012. Old GM shareholders got nothing.
lines.say: Lehman filed in two thousand eight; its shares were cancelled in twenty twelve. Old GM shareholders got nothing.

lines.text: Hertz in 2021 was rare: creditors got paid in full, so shareholders got value.
lines.say: Hertz in twenty twenty-one was rare: creditors got paid in full, so shareholders got value.

lines.text: SIPC covers up to $500,000 if your broker fails, not if your stock does.

post.title: What happens to your stock when a company goes bankrupt
post.ig:
Own a stock that goes bankrupt? Shareholders get paid dead last.
The SEC says stockholders are last in line, after secured creditors and unsecured creditors like bondholders.
In Chapter 11, the plan often cancels old shares and new stock goes to creditors.
S&P Global counted 785 large US corporate bankruptcies in 2025, the most since 2010.
SIPC (up to $500,000, including $250,000 cash) covers a failed brokerage, not a stock losing value.
Sources: SEC/Investor.gov, FINRA, SIPC, S&P Global Market Intelligence, company filings.
News and education, not financial advice.
